title: Benchmark
intro: A labelled set of made-up scenarios, run through Noa's real rules in your browser, right now. Each scenario carries the outcome that Noa's published rule table asks for. Noa's own answer is compared with it, step by step.

honest.title: What this is, and what it is not
honest.noise: Sensor noise is switched off in the benchmark, so the heart rate typed in is exactly the reading. The playback in the other tabs adds a few beats of noise, but never across the 120 line, so both give the same answer.
honest.body: This checks that Noa follows its own published rules, including at the edge of each threshold and on messy input. The scenarios are synthetic and were labelled by hand from the rule table. It is not clinical validation: it does not show that the rules are medically right, and it was not tested on patients.

run.label: Benchmark progress
run.idle: Not run yet. The list at the bottom shows every scenario and what the rule table expects.

crit.title: The decision that matters most: 998 now
crit.intro: Counted over the {{n}} safety scenarios that reach a decision. Positive means the rule table says to call 998 now. A missed emergency is the error that matters; a false alarm is the cheaper one.
crit.sensHelp: Emergencies Noa sent to 998, out of all emergencies
crit.specHelp: Non-emergencies Noa kept out of 998, out of all non-emergencies
crit.matrixLabel: Confusion matrix: rule table against Noa's decision

groups.title: Accuracy by group
groups.intro: A scenario counts as matching only when the sensor rule, the deciding rule, the decision and the agent all agree with the rule table.

group.people: The same rules for every person
group.family-forecast: Family heart score, F1 and F2

rules.title: Accuracy by rule
rules.intro: Each rule is tested where it should fire and where it must hold back. R1 to R4 start a check; R5 to R12 decide.

sub.title: Subgroups
sub.intro: The same rules should give the same answers however the scenario is tagged. The 998 columns cover the safety scenarios only.

fail.title: Where Noa and the rule table differ
fail.none: No differences. Every scenario that ran matches the rule table.
fail.intro: Nothing is hidden or fixed here: each line says what the rule table expects, what Noa did, and which step and agent diverged first.

table.title: All scenarios
table.intro: Filter the list, and open a scenario as a case in the Test case tab to see Noa work through it.
table.searchHint: Id or words in the title

limits.title: Limits, in plain words
limits.a: The scenarios are synthetic and few. A perfect score on {{n}} made-up cases says Noa follows its rules; it says nothing about how often the rules are right for real people.
limits.b: The expected outcomes come from the published rule table and the prototype's demo thresholds, which are not clinical guidance. The labels were written by the team, not by an independent clinician.
limits.c: The intervals are 95% Wilson intervals. With these counts they are wide for small groups: read them before reading the percentages.
limits.d: The speech check is a demo score (words matched and time taken), not a validated stroke test.
